messages.subject: Re: Help with CJS Constant Survival Model
parts:
John, it looks like you have a typo (JAGS is case-sensitive). The pertinent parts of the error message are:

“Unknown variable nInd” – meaning nInd is used in the model statement but not provided in the data; and

“Unused variable "nind" in data” – meaning nind is supplied in the data but not used in the model statement.

If nInd and nind are referring to the same thing, changing nInd in the model statement to nind (all lower-case) should fix it.

You might want to check your use of "f" and "n.occasions" as well, as apparently those are also supplied as data but not used in the model statement (won't cause a fatal error, only a warning, but might indicate that you haven't done what you intended to do with the model).

Cheers,

Emily

On Fri, Jul 24, 2020 at 11:49 AM john.hu...@gmail.com <john.hu...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi All,
I have a encounter history with 82 individuals and capture data was collected over three years. When adapting the CJS Constant Parameter model code provided for JAGS from Kery and Schaub(2012), I get the error when calling JAGS from R:

"Error in jags.model(file = model.file, data = data, inits = inits, n.chains = n.chains, : RUNTIME ERROR: Compilation error on line 8. Unknown variable nInd Either supply values for this variable with the data or define it on the left hand side of a relation. In addition: Warning messages: 1: In jags.model(file = model.file, data = data, inits = inits, n.chains = n.chains, : Unused variable "f" in data 2: In jags.model(file = model.file, data = data, inits = inits, n.chains = n.chains, : Unused variable "nind" in data 3: In jags.model(file = model.file, data = data, inits = inits, n.chains = n.chains, : Unused variable "n.occasions" in data"

Can anyone help me please? I can provide more code if needed.

Thank you in advance!

John
